name: LevelCheck clinical cohort (De Silva 2016, Johns Hopkins)
what: intraoperative spine radiographs with the same patient's preoperative CT, the vertebral levels placed on each radiograph by registration to the labelled CT (De Silva et al., Spine 2016; Ketcha et al. 2017; the reader images of Manbachi et al. 2018)
level_truth: yes, every vertebra's level registered from the labelled CT
status: refused: asked Jeffrey Siewerdsen on 2026-10-21, who answered the same day that the data are held at Johns Hopkins, which he has left, and pointed to Ali Uneri; asked Uneri on 2026-10-21, who answered on 2026-10-23 that the cohort's IRB approval expired years ago and that Hopkins' IRB now restricts sharing patient data across institutions; he suggested the Harms Study Group (hsg.settingscoliosisstraight.org), a multi-institution scoliosis dataset whose imaging he could not vouch for, and offered to introduce the owner to its administrators; the owner accepted on 2026-10-23 16:56 UTC, dropping LevelCheck and noting that the site describes the AIS registry and a Database User Program but not whether the radiographs themselves are shared with a research user; the introduction has not come by 2026-10-25
licence: not shared (Johns Hopkins IRB approval expired)
how_to_get: None: the holder refused on 2026-10-23. The alternative Uneri named is the Harms Study Group (hsg.settingscoliosisstraight.org); the owner asked him for the introduction on 2026-10-23, and once it comes, the question for its administrators is whether the radiographs can be shared with a research user.
